$comment: What one section of a textbook yields, read out by a model: the concepts it names, how they stand to one another, what its figures show, and the terms it defines. The document twin of extraction.schema.json -- same shape (arrays of flat objects, relations as from/rel/to) so entities.fold folds it and the graph builder takes it without a second reader. A field the section does not give is an empty string, never a guess; `rel` is a closed vocabulary because an open one drifts into fourteen spellings of `part_of` inside one book.

name.$comment: As the section writes it, singular where the section is.

kind.$comment: `unit` is a unit of measurement; `law` a named law, principle or theorem; `structure` a thing with parts (an organ, an organelle, a machine); `process` something that happens over time. Anything the section names that fits none of these is a `concept`.

definition.$comment: One line, in the book's own words, only when the section defines it. Empty otherwise -- a definition invented here is the failure this field exists to make visible.

aliases.$comment: Other names the section itself uses for the same thing: a plural, an abbreviation, a symbol.

rel.$comment: A closed vocabulary: fourteen verb phrases that between them say what a textbook says. Nothing outside it, and nothing the section does not state.

label.$comment: The book's own name for it, e.g. "Figure 2.9"; empty when the section gives none.

shows.$comment: What the picture shows, in one line.

concepts.$comment: Only the concepts the caption or the surrounding text says the figure illustrates. A concept guessed from the picture alone does not belong here.
